questions.question: The capital for a new venture is allocated to Technology, Marketing, and Operations in the ratio 4 : 3 : 1. During the first quarter, the cost of Technology rose by 10%, Marketing fell by 5%, and Operations rose by 20%. What is the percent change (increase or decrease) in the total capital required?
questions.questionHtml: The capital for a new venture is allocated to Technology, Marketing, and Operations in the ratio 4 : 3 : 1. During the first quarter, the cost of Technology rose by 10%, Marketing fell by 5%, and Operations rose by 20%. What is the percent change (increase or decrease) in the total capital required?
questions.solution:
Let total capital = 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 units

Technology new = 4 + 10% of 4 = 4 + 0.4 = 4.4

Marketing new = 3 − 5% of 3 = 3 − 0.15 = 2.85

Operations new = 1 + 20% of 1 = 1 + 0.2 = 1.2

New total = 4.4 + 2.85 + 1.2 = 8.45

% change = ((8.45 − 8) ÷ 8) × 100 = 5.625%

questions.question: A buyer ordered 12 kg of premium sugar and some standard sugar. The price of premium sugar per kg was three times that of the standard sugar. Due to an ordering error, the quantities of the two types of sugar were interchanged. This decreased the total cost by 25%. Find the ratio of the quantity of premium sugar to standard sugar in the original order.
questions.questionHtml: A buyer ordered 12 kg of premium sugar and some standard sugar. The price of premium sugar per kg was three times that of the standard sugar. Due to an ordering error, the quantities of the two types of sugar were interchanged. This decreased the total cost by 25%. Find the ratio of the quantity of premium sugar to standard sugar in the original order.
questions.solution:
Let price of premium = 3p, price of standard = p.

Original cost = 12 × 3p + x × p = 36p + xp.

New cost = 12 × p + x × 3p = 12p + 3xp.

Decrease = 25% of original ⇒ (36p + xp) − (12p + 3xp) = (1/4)(36p + xp).

24p − 2xp = (1/4)(36p + xp) ⇒ 96p − 8xp = 36p + xp.

60p = 9xp ⇒ x = 60 ÷ 9 = 20/3.

Premium : Standard = 12 : 20/3 = 36 : 20 = 9 : 5.

∴ Required ratio = 9 : 5.

questions.question: P and Q together can complete a work in 10 days. Q and R together can complete the same work in 15 days. R and P together can do it in 30 days. In how many days can Q alone complete the job?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q together can complete a work in 10 days. Q and R together can complete the same work in 15 days. R and P together can do it in 30 days. In how many days can Q alone complete the job?
questions.solution:
Let the total work be the LCM of 10, 15, and 30.

⇒ LCM(10, 15, 30) = 30 units.

Work done by P + Q in 1 day = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units.

Work done by Q + R in 1 day = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units.

Work done by R + P in 1 day = 30 ÷ 30 = 1 unit.

Adding all: (P + Q) + (Q + R) + (R + P) = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units.

⇒ 2(P + Q + R) = 6 ⇒ P + Q + R = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 units.

For Q: (P + Q + R) − (R + P) = 3 − 1 = 2 units.

Total days = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 days.

∴ The correct answer is 15 days.

questions.question: A vendor sold 15 items for 3600 and gained a profit of 20%. How many items should he sell for 4320 to make a profit of 8%?
questions.questionHtml: A vendor sold 15 items for 3600 and gained a profit of 20%. How many items should he sell for 4320 to make a profit of 8%?
questions.solution:
⇒ CP of 15 items = 3600 ÷ 1.20 = 3000

⇒ CP of 1 item = 3000 ÷ 15 = 200

⇒ SP per item (for 8% profit) = 200 × 1.08 = 216

⇒ Number of items = 4320 ÷ 216 = 20

questions.question: A juice vendor mixes water with pure fruit concentrate. If he sells the mixture at the cost price of pure concentrate and makes a profit of 30%, what is the ratio of water to pure concentrate in the mixture, respectively?
questions.questionHtml: A juice vendor mixes water with pure fruit concentrate. If he sells the mixture at the cost price of pure concentrate and makes a profit of 30%, what is the ratio of water to pure concentrate in the mixture, respectively?
questions.solution:
⇒ Selling Price = 1.3 × Cost Price

⇒ Concentrate proportion = 1 ÷ 1.3, Water proportion = 1 − (1 ÷ 1.3)

⇒ Ratio = (0.3 ÷ 1.3) : (1 ÷ 1.3) = 0.3 : 1 = 3 : 10

questions.question: From an 80-liter container of pure milk, 10 liters are removed and replaced by water. This operation is performed a total of three times. What is the final quantity of milk remaining in the container?
questions.questionHtml: From an 80-liter container of pure milk, 10 liters are removed and replaced by water. This operation is performed a total of three times. What is the final quantity of milk remaining in the container?
questions.solution:
Milk remaining after 3 operations = 80 × (1 − (10 ÷ 80))3

= 80 × (0.875)3

= 80 × 0.669921875 ≈ 53.6 liters

questions.question: A and B are running around a park's circular track which has a perimeter of 2.4 km. They start from the same point at 7:00 a.m. and run in opposite directions. A's speed is 8 km/h, and B's speed is 10 km/h. At what time will they meet for the third time?
questions.questionHtml: A and B are running around a park's circular track which has a perimeter of 2.4 km. They start from the same point at 7:00 a.m. and run in opposite directions. A's speed is 8 km/h, and B's speed is 10 km/h. At what time will they meet for the third time?
questions.solution:
Perimeter = 2.4 km, Relative speed = 8 + 10 = 18 km/h.

Time interval = 2.4 ÷ 18 = 0.133333... hours ⇒ 0.133333... × 60 = 8 minutes.

Meeting times: 1st = 7:00 + 8 min = 7:08, 2nd = 7:08 + 8 min = 7:16, 3rd = 7:16 + 8 min = 7:24.

questions.question: A car covers 60% of a certain distance at a pace of 40 km/h and the remaining distance at a pace of 60 km/h. What is the average speed of the car for the entire journey?
questions.questionHtml: A car covers 60% of a certain distance at a pace of 40 km/h and the remaining distance at a pace of 60 km/h. What is the average speed of the car for the entire journey?
questions.solution:
Let the total distance be D.

Time for first part = 0.6D ÷ 40 = 0.015D

Time for second part = 0.4D ÷ 60 = 0.00667D

Total Time = 0.015D + 0.00667D = 0.02167D

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = D ÷ 0.02167D = 46.15 km/h

questions.question: What is the radian measure of 210°?
questions.questionHtml: What is the radian measure of 210°?
questions.solution:
Radian measure = (π ÷ 180) × 210

⇒ Radian measure = (210 ÷ 180) × π

⇒ Radian measure = 7π ÷ 6

questions.question: In triangles PQR and STU, if angle P equals angle S, side PQ equals side ST, and angle Q equals angle T, which congruence rule demonstrates that triangle PQR is congruent to triangle STU?
questions.questionHtml: In triangles PQR and STU, if angle P equals angle S, side PQ equals side ST, and angle Q equals angle T, which congruence rule demonstrates that triangle PQR is congruent to triangle STU?
questions.solution:
⇒ Angle P = Angle S

⇒ Side PQ = Side ST (included side)

⇒ Angle Q = Angle T

∴ Triangles PQR and STU satisfy the ASA Congruence Rule.

questions.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral MNOP, if angle N is 115°, what is the measure of angle P?
questions.questionHtml: In a cyclic quadrilateral MNOP, if angle N is 115°, what is the measure of angle P?
questions.solution:
Angle N + Angle P = 180º

115º + Angle P = 180º

Angle P = 180º − 115º = 65º

questions.question: If cos 2 (A) - sin 2 (A) = 3/5, find the value of sin 2 (A).
questions.questionHtml: If cos<sup>2</sup>(A) - sin<sup>2</sup>(A) = 3/5, find the value of sin<sup>2</sup>(A).
questions.solution:
cos2A − sin2A = 3/5

⇒ (1 − sin2A) − sin2A = 3/5

⇒ 1 − 2sin2A = 3/5

⇒ 2/5 = 2sin2A

⇒ sin2A = 1/5
